title: Article 99 — Oath or affirmation by members

content.overview: Article 99 requires every member of either House of Parliament to make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by the President, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out for the purpose in the Third Schedule, before taking his seat.
content.glance: Every MP must take Third Schedule oath/affirmation before the President (or person appointed by President) before taking seat.
content.study:
Article 99 is the seating-oath requirement for members of Parliament. The form is in the Third Schedule. The oath is made before the President or a person appointed by the President.

Examination: before taking seat; Third Schedule form; before President or appointee.

sections.heading: Key rule
sections.body: Before taking his seat, every member of either House shall make and subscribe the Third Schedule oath or affirmation before the President or a person appointed by the President.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When and before whom does a member of Parliament take the oath?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 99, every member of either House of Parliament shall, before taking his seat, make and subscribe before the President, or some person appointed in that behalf by the President, an oath or affirmation according to the form set out in the Third Schedule.

examTips: Oath before taking seat; Third Schedule; before President or appointee.

keyTakeaways: Art 99: Third Schedule oath before taking seat.
